criteria.criterion: For both the bash and powershell tools, pwsh and powershell accept only the pinned literal -Command/-c form after the allowed pre-options, judge every remaining word joined with spaces as a powershell call, preserve the phase and root, and count each wrapper toward the eight-level nesting limit.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/expand.go:200 advances past -ExecutionPolicy's value without checking exp; an expanded structural value is accepted and can inject additional pwsh arguments. Literal command joining, phase/root reuse, and the depth boundary otherwise appear in expand.go:205-224, judge.go:384-398 and wrappers_test.go:79-103.

criteria.criterion: Missing, expanded, encoded, file, stdin, bare-script and unsupported-option pwsh forms fail closed with the exact W1 reasons, including the wrapper's written pwsh or powershell name where specified.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/expand.go:193-242 implements the listed refusal branches, and wrappers_test.go:15-45 checks the missing command-string, expanded command string, stdin, file, bare-script, encoded and unsupported-option reasons through both outer tools.

criteria.criterion: cmd accepts only /c or /k after /d, /q and /s, judges its literal string split at &, &&, || and |, and denies % or ^; every other cmd form fails closed with the exact W1 reason.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/judge.go:278-287 sends each splitCMD part through splitPowerShell, whose lexer also splits at ';' and newline (split.go:314-317); cmd therefore does not implement the pinned four-operator grammar. cmdString does enforce its pre-options and literal command expansion, and shellMode denies % and ^.

criteria.criterion: A command inside a wrapper is allowed or denied exactly as the same command in the wrapped tool would be, including case-insensitive command and option matching and names with a path or .exe.
criteria.evidence: A cmd string is judged by the PowerShell lexer (judge.go:281), so cmd /c "echo ok; git push" is split into a denied second PowerShell statement although ';' is literal in cmd. Conversely, a direct command under cmd's specified wrapped semantics is not matched with the same result.

criteria.criterion: Committed Go tests cover the allowed and refused wrapper forms, option and name variants, command matching, nesting, phase/root preservation and both outer tools, and the go check executes them.
criteria.evidence: internal/fence/wrappers_test.go covers both outer tools, wrapper spellings/options/paths, allowed and refused forms, command matching, phase/root writes and the nesting boundary; .vloop/tmp/checks.json's go check exited 0 and its log runs internal/fence successfully.

findings.summary: pwsh -ExecutionPolicy accepts an expanded value without refusing it, so structural argument expansion can inject options that the fence never judges.
cmd command strings are reparsed as PowerShell, adding semicolon and newline separators that the W1 cmd grammar explicitly excludes and changing the wrapper's decisions.

notes: The committed tests should pin an expanded -ExecutionPolicy/-ep value and a semicolon/newline inside cmd /c so these fail-closed and grammar-parity gaps cannot regress.
